services.name: Cloud Storage

persistence.restartBehavior: Survives process and container restart while the LocalCloud volume is retained
recoveryLimitations: No production durability or replication semantics.

limitations: [partial] Bucket policy APIs use gateway 5380/TLS 5381. Object authorization is enforced at both direct listeners and the gateway when IAM mode requires it.
[partial] gcp-live uses caller-token Google permission checks with no fallback. Real-Google and object-conditional grant qualification remain pending; unsupported remote grants fail closed.
[partial] Open mode deliberately permits known-bucket access; project listing uses authoritative ownership and is not an open-mode tenant security boundary.
[partial] Notification delivery uses precreated local Pub/Sub topics. Persisted messages retry after failure/restart; ordering and transactional object/outbox crash atomicity are not promised.

[unsupported] Filesystem-backed buckets do not support versioning or OBJECT_ARCHIVE notifications. Finalize, metadata-update and delete delivery are live-container qualified; versioning is a separate development gap, not production-only.

[partial] HMAC supports local project-ID-scoped service-account identities. Project-number aliases and default-compute identities are not resolved; real-Google gcp-live impersonation is not qualified. Secrets are excluded from project YAML exports; encrypted key state is retained in full filesystem snapshots.
[prod_only] Object lifecycle scheduling, retention policies and retention enforcement are production-only and excluded from developer completeness.
[unsupported] Managed-folder APIs are not implemented.

[partial] Bucket metadata: buckets.insert, patch, update (PUT) and get keep labels, uniform bucket-level access, public access prevention, location, storage class and metageneration, and patch/update honor ifMetagenerationMatch. Lifecycle, CORS, website, logging, retention, soft-delete, hierarchical-namespace, RPO, encryption, billing and Autoclass fields are accepted but not stored or returned. projectNumber is always 0, so import buckets into Terraform as project/bucket; a bare-name import falls back to the provider's default project.

[partial] Path-style HMAC XML requests accept localhost and loopback IPs with discovered Docker ports. Virtual-host requests use the configured public hostname (localhost); signed Host headers must not be rewritten after signing.

[partial] LocalCloud's own Storage work (seed, reset, remote-sync import and manifest cleanup, project checkpoints and migration fixtures) runs as LocalCloud with a process-local internal credential, so strict and gcp-live policies do not block it; sync refuses a bucket another local project owns. Console browse, mutation and export keep the caller's identity, and Workflows Storage connectors run as the workflow's service account (the Workflows service agent when none is set). A reset whose Storage listing or deletes the running emulator rejects reports partial_failure, and a failed sync-manifest cleanup keeps the manifest; an unreachable emulator is still treated as having nothing to reset.

[partial] Local live-container HTTP qualification includes multipart uploads, admin caller propagation, strict signed IAM, notification recovery and reset. These fixes require a rebuilt image; trusted release-image and full LocalCloud TLS qualification remain pending.

services.name: Pub/Sub

persistence.restartBehavior: Topics, subscriptions, and queued messages persist in PostgreSQL. Delivery workers and active connections restart; qualify the exact replay and redelivery workflow.
recoveryLimitations: A mounted volume does not provide production delivery, replication, or recovery guarantees; qualify the assembled image.

limitations: Exactly-once delivery, export subscriptions, transforms, PushConfig attributes and payload wrappers, and other unlisted advanced fields remain unsupported.

Authenticated push tokens are signed by the LocalCloud issuer (/identity/status, keys at /oauth2/v3/certs), not https://accounts.google.com; receivers must trust the local JWKS. Revoking the Pub/Sub service agent's token-creator role is not modeled.
Retry dispatch and retention cleanup are approximate local schedules; this does not reproduce Google production scale, availability or service-agent IAM.
Schema definitions must be self-contained; imported protobuf types are unsupported, matching the Pub/Sub schema restriction.

Stored Pub/Sub IAM policies can be read and evaluated through IAM APIs, but publish and topic deletion do not enforce those resource bindings. Strict mode and successful testIamPermissions do not establish Pub/Sub data-plane authorization.

operations.label: retention, snapshot CRUD, timestamp and snapshot seek

operations.label: schema and revision lifecycle, validation, publish enforcement
limitations: Avro 1.11 and proto2/proto3, JSON/binary, revision ranges, and atomic publish batches.

operations.label: PushConfig oidcToken on create/update/modifyPushConfig, signed push delivery
limitations: google.pubsub.v1 PushConfig.OidcToken (proto-google-cloud-pubsub-v1 1.157.0) is accepted over REST and gRPC, persisted in the subscription and returned on readback. Each push attempt sends one Authorization: Bearer ID token from the LocalCloud issuer for serviceAccountEmail, with the email claim and the configured audience or, when empty, the exact push endpoint URL. In enforcing IAM modes (strict, gcp-live), setting it requires iam.serviceAccounts.actAs on the account. The Pub/Sub service agent's token-creator grant is modeled as Google's default; revoking it is not. If no token can be minted (account missing, disabled or identity not ready), the message is not sent and follows the normal NACK, retry and dead-letter path, and LocalCloud logs IDENTITY_UNAVAILABLE:<reason>; sibling subscriptions on the topic are unaffected. Google requires an explicit token-creator grant to the service agent only for projects that enabled Pub/Sub on or before 2021-04-08, so a missing agent grant cannot occur locally. A non-2xx endpoint response is a NACK: the message is redelivered with a freshly minted token. The actAs check is component-tested in strict mode. Partial until the packaged-image receipt test has run against a candidate image.

services.name: Bigtable

persistence.restartBehavior: LocalCloud Docker is intended to retain PostgreSQL-backed service data while the mounted /var/lib/localcloud volume is retained
recoveryLimitations: The machine-local cached artifact can use PostgreSQL or SQLite, but the LocalCloud Docker product is configured for PostgreSQL.
Dependency identity, restart recovery, and the assembled LocalCloud image remain release-unverified.

limitations: The pinned little_bigtable dd5f9e7 (v0.5.0) passes its dependency test suite, and its executable ledger covers all 89 registered RPCs. That evidence is for the dependency source, not LocalCloud. It ran on SQLite rather than LocalCloud's PostgreSQL backend and skipped the pinned cbt test. The 2026-10-05 UTC arm64 candidate (sha256:2bd0813e574ddf6af1bfd9be6f3b318e6290117b4c5fc1142d651de5d274b754) embeds this revision and completed platform testing with two failing Bigtable cases (project deletion and backup listing). The LocalCloud fixes for both pass BigtablePlatformTest with a source JAR over that image; exact-image and full LocalCloud Bigtable qualification remain open.
IAM policies persist but are not enforced. TestIamPermissions grants every requested permission because the emulator is unauthenticated; the direct gRPC listener also bypasses gateway IAM.

Change streams use one partition with no split or merge. last_scanned_row_key is not emitted, logical views do not support view parameters, query statistics are not recorded, and google.cloud.location.Locations is not served.
HLL++ aggregate sketch bytes and multi-column materialized-view row keys use emulator-specific encodings that are not byte-compatible with production.

Legacy table snapshot RPCs (SnapshotTable, GetSnapshot, ListSnapshots, DeleteSnapshot, CreateTableFromSnapshot) return Unimplemented; they are a deprecated private-alpha API. Use backups for data protection.

The Console REST admin facade ignores emulator errors on row writes and deletes and on app-profile and view routes, then reports success from local placeholder state. Instance PATCH/PUT and table PATCH answer locally without reaching the emulator, and logical and materialized view updates drop their update masks. Verify through the native API when a result must reflect emulator validation.

assembledDefault.limitation: Default enablement follows the current runtime catalog and remains subject to license-tier gates.

operations.label: instances/tables/families
limitations: The pinned little_bigtable dd5f9e7 (v0.5.0) emulates instance, cluster, app-profile, table and schema-bundle administration as validated metadata (ID and field rules, response views, update masks, pagination, deletion protection, soft delete and 7-day undelete, atomic column-family changes, initial splits, row key schema) with a durable long-running-operation registry. Cluster nodes and autoscaling settings are stored without capacity effects. Dependency conformance tests pass; LocalCloud image qualification of this revision is pending.

operations.label: row mutations and reads
limitations: dd5f9e7 validates every mutation before applying any (single-row atomicity), reports real per-entry MutateRows codes, honors idempotency tokens and aggregate (Sum/Min/Max, HLL++) families, implements every RowFilter including Interleave duplicates, Sink (cells bypass subsequent filters; invalid inside Condition) and ValueBitmask, chunks ReadRows like production with request stats, samples SampleRowKeys within row ranges, enforces authorized-view, materialized-view and app-profile targets, and serves the OpenTable/OpenAuthorizedView/OpenMaterializedView session protocol. last_scanned_row_key is not emitted. Sink output and rejection inside Condition have named dependency conformance tests; a dedicated LocalCloud Sink platform scenario is pending. Dependency conformance tests pass; LocalCloud image qualification is pending.

operations.label: cbt CLI compatibility
limitations:
The `cbt` CLI works with BIGTABLE_EMULATOR_HOST env var.
Arbitrary project and instance IDs are accepted on-demand without pre-registration, matching Google Cloud SDK CBT emulator behavior.
The gRPC data plane accepts requests without an authorization header or credential provider.
Instance CRUD (create/list/get/delete instance) is supported via gRPC.
Table and row operations work as expected.
Not re-run against little_bigtable dd5f9e7: its pinned cbt conformance test was skipped because cbt was not installed, so this rests on earlier evidence until the LocalCloud image is qualified.

operations.label: localcloud console data browser
limitations:
REST endpoints for instance/table/row CRUD exposed via BigtableAdminService:
- GET  /.../tables/{table}/rows — browse rows
- POST /.../tables/{table}/rows — write cells
- DELETE /.../tables/{table}/rows/{rowKey} — delete row
SDK and console share the same PostgreSQL-backed emulator state.
Instance, table and backup routes forward to the emulator and return its errors with the Google API HTTP mapping (FAILED_PRECONDITION as 400, for example). Row writes and deletes, app-profile and view routes still ignore emulator errors and report success from local placeholder state, and instance PATCH/PUT and table PATCH answer locally without reaching the emulator, so a rejected request on those routes can appear to succeed.

operations.label: data survives emulator restart
limitations: dd5f9e7 persists all resource state in PostgreSQL, including table policy fields, views, schema bundles, backups and their row snapshots, IAM policies, long-running operations, the change-stream outbox and idempotency tokens. On first start it migrates table metadata in place (one-way). Its restart tests ran on SQLite; PostgreSQL restart durability in the LocalCloud image is pending.

operations.label: materialized views (CMVs)
limitations: dd5f9e7 implements continuous materialized views from GoogleSQL GROUP BY or ORDER BY definitions over existing tables. Views are read-only, read through materialized_view_name (ReadRows, SampleRowKeys, sessions) or GoogleSQL, recomputed before a read when stale, limited to 50 per instance and 5 per source table, and their query is immutable. Multi-column row-key encoding is emulator-specific. LocalCloud image qualification is pending.

operations.label: GoogleSQL queries and logical views
limitations: dd5f9e7 builds its GoogleSQL engine by default. PrepareQuery returns a prepared-query token valid for one hour; ExecuteQuery streams typed ProtoRows batches with CRC32C checksums and resume tokens, and returns FailedPrecondition (PREPARED_QUERY_EXPIRED) after a schema change. Logical-view queries are validated against existing tables and are queryable. Query statistics and view parameters are not emulated. LocalCloud image qualification is pending; the Console SQL editor uses LocalCloud's separate translator.

operations.label: change streams
limitations: dd5f9e7 records changes only for tables with change_stream_config (1-7 day retention). ReadChangeStream returns one grouped record per row commit, garbage-collection and DropRowRange records, heartbeats with continuation tokens and low watermarks, resumes from tokens and closes at end_time. It requires a single-cluster app profile. One partition covers the whole key space, so partition split and merge are not exercised. LocalCloud image qualification is pending.

operations.label: snapshots and backups
limitations: dd5f9e7 backups are immutable schema-and-row snapshots with create, get, list (filter, order, pagination), update, copy, delete and restore to a new table independent of the live source, including expire-time, backup-type and quota rules. UndeleteTable restores a deleted table within 7 days. Legacy table snapshot RPCs return Unimplemented because they are a deprecated private-alpha API. The LocalCloud REST facade forwards backup create, get, list, update (with the required updateMask), copy, delete, restore and undelete to the emulator and returns its errors. LocalCloud image qualification is pending.

operations.label: IAM policy management
limitations: dd5f9e7 persists policies on existing Bigtable resources with etags (Aborted on mismatch) and update masks, and returns NotFound for missing resources. Policies are permissive. TestIamPermissions grants every requested permission and nothing is enforced on the direct gRPC listener, because the emulator is unauthenticated.

operations.label: new proto methods return Unimplemented (no panics)
limitations: The dd5f9e7 executable ledger dispositions all 89 registered RPCs of the cloud.google.com/go/bigtable v1.58.0 interface, and a test fails if one is missing. Intentionally unsupported RPCs (legacy snapshots, hot tablets, memory layers) return Unimplemented instead of panicking. PingAndWarm validates the instance name and app profile.

services.name: Spanner

persistence.backingStore: LevelDB rows plus JSON metadata at /var/lib/localcloud/spanner-data
persistence.restartBehavior: Ordinary container stop/start retains state; a mounted /var/lib/localcloud volume is required to retain state across container removal or replacement
recoveryLimitations: Rows use LevelDB and metadata uses JSON files.
Known corruption/recovery risk; internal safety snapshots are not Cloud Spanner Backup API.

limitations: Extended Spanner emulator image supports 140 features (1 partial [schema.queues], 8 accepted-no-op, 9 production-only exclusions, 0 unsupported out of 158 feature records). Public-endpoint client matrix is 100% verified against native builds and packaged Docker image with Python (3.71.0), Go (1.95.1), Node.js (9.0.0), Java (6.123.0), JDBC (2.45.0), and PGAdapter (0.55.3 with pgJDBC and psql).

Database roles and fine-grained access control (FGAC) are enforced for sessions created with a creator_role. Unauthenticated emulator connections bypass IAM principal identity checks; stored IAM policies do not enforce network identity.
Change streams require ExecuteStreamingSql; unary ExecuteSql rejects change-stream queries. With --data_dir, stream definitions, records, partition history, and resume tokens survive restarts.
Backups require --data_dir; each backup is a full database copy. Customer-managed encryption keys (CMEK) are not implemented (data is plaintext).

Production-only infrastructure exclusions (Google TrueTime hardware clock, multi-region Paxos quorum switching, physical split points and tablet distribution, physical cross-region migration, multi-tenant compute slicing) do not apply to local development.

assembledDefault.limitation: Default enablement follows the current runtime catalog and remains subject to license-tier gates.

operations.label: Native SQL, read, and streaming read
limitations: Native ExecuteSql and ExecuteStreamingSql in both GoogleSQL and PostgreSQL dialects. StreamingRead and ExecuteStreamingSql stream whole rows with resume tokens at row boundaries. Unary ExecuteSql intentionally retains the emulator's rejection of change-stream queries. Full-text search (TOKENIZE_*, SEARCH, SNIPPET, SCORE), vector search (APPROX_* / ScaNN), and 13 graph algorithms (PageRank, ShortestPath, etc.) compute locally.

operations.label: Sessions, transactions, and batch DML
limitations: Sessions (including batch create and multiplexed), read-write, read-only and single-use transactions. SERIALIZABLE (default) and REPEATABLE_READ isolation. Conflicts follow wound-wait lock waits (--lock_wait_timeout_ms). Exclusive locks via SELECT ... FOR UPDATE and LOCK_SCANNED_RANGES=exclusive. Commit timestamps (PENDING_COMMIT_TIMESTAMP) and commit stats (mutation count). Deadlock aborts exactly one transaction. Unique indexes are re-checked at commit.

operations.label: Partition query/read and batch write
limitations: PartitionRead, PartitionQuery, partitioned DML (including parameterized PostgreSQL statements), and BatchWrite are supported.

operations.label: Instance, configuration, and instance-partition administration
limitations: Instance and instance-partition administration, custom instance configurations, and MoveInstance (metadata). List operations and instances support AIP-160 filter expressions.

operations.label: Database administration and DDL
limitations: Database creation, DDL execution for both GoogleSQL and PostgreSQL, drop protection (UpdateDatabase), ListDatabaseOperations, split points (AddSplitPoints persisted to SPANNER_SYS.USER_SPLIT_POINTS), and fine-grained access control database roles (CREATE/DROP ROLE, GRANT/REVOKE, ListDatabaseRoles).

operations.label: Instance and database IAM policies
limitations: IAM policies are stored durably in LevelDB and returned through native endpoints with etags guarded. Fine-grained access control (FGAC) is enforced for sessions created with a creator_role on queries, DML, reads, mutations, and change stream reads. Unauthenticated emulator connections bypass network IAM.

operations.label: Backup, copy, restore, and backup schedules
limitations: With --data_dir, CreateBackup, CopyBackup, GetBackup, ListBackups (with AIP-160 filter precedence), UpdateBackup, DeleteBackup, RestoreDatabase, and ListBackupOperations are supported. version_time backups and full/incremental backup schedules persist cursors across restarts.

operations.label: Long-running operation lifecycle
limitations: Native long-running operations lifecycle across instance, database, backup, copy, and restore calls, with AIP-160 filter support.

persistence.restartBehavior: Queues, task bodies, and task state are reloaded after restart while the LocalCloud volume is retained

limitations: Task and queue OAuth/OIDC credentials are minted by the LocalCloud issuer, not Google, and verify only against LocalCloud's JWKS. A queue httpTarget credential overrides task credentials and every task Authorization header; at queue level both the service account and the audience/scope are required. OIDC audience defaults to the full task URL and OAuth scope to cloud-platform. Each attempt mints through the delivery token cache; when no token can be minted (for example, a disabled or deleted account) the request is not sent and the attempt records IDENTITY_UNAVAILABLE:<reason> with normal retry semantics. Strict and gcp-live modes require iam.serviceAccounts.actAs on the account when a task or queue is configured; the account is not checked against the queue's project. Redirect responses are not followed.
App Engine delivery, queue httpTarget uriOverride/httpMethod/headerOverrides and logging sampling are rejected as unsupported rather than silently stored.

No FIFO, exactly-once, dead-letter queue, transactional cancellation, adaptive Google throttling or production throughput guarantees. Removed task IDs have no Google-style deduplication tombstone. Unlimited retry settings have no automatic task-retention expiry.

HTTP attempt deadlines are durations from 15 to 1800 seconds (default 600). Failed attempts use configured fractional backoff; finite attempt and duration bounds must both be exhausted. A zero duration leaves only the attempt limit; -1 attempts is unlimited.

Local activity retains completed attempt metadata for seven days, with no request URL, headers, payload or response body archive. Interrupted or unpersisted outcomes may remain unknown. Successful/terminal tasks leave the active queue; absence alone is not success.

Pending and interrupted in-flight tasks recover after restart with possible redelivery. Pause, purge and deletion do not cancel requests already in flight. Never replay an ambiguous create or run request automatically.

BASIC omits payload, headers and the OAuth/OIDC configuration; FULL requires cloudtasks.tasks.fullView in enforcing IAM modes. Queue/task operations evaluate stored allow policies in strict and gcp-live modes; open/permissive modes do not enforce them.

limitations: Five-field UNIX cron uses the installed cron-utils parser and Java IANA zones. Preview and dispatch share that parser. HTTP and Pub/Sub delivery are implemented. App Engine configurations are rejected before saving; managed App Engine execution is unavailable.

httpTarget oidcToken and oauthToken are stored with the job and minted at each attempt by the local issuer, not Google. The OIDC audience defaults to the full target URI including the query; the OAuth scope defaults to cloud-platform. The generated header is the only Authorization header; a user Authorization header stays rejected. Receivers must trust the local issuer and JWKS. In strict and gcp-live, create and every update of a job carrying a token need iam.serviceAccounts.actAs on its account; a missing account is reported as the same denial. At delivery a missing, deleted or disabled account (or unavailable issuer) fails the attempt with IDENTITY_UNAVAILABLE:<reason> through normal retry and history, and the request is not sent. Revoking the Scheduler service agent is not modeled.

Queued runs and retries survive restart. An attempt interrupted while RUNNING becomes UNKNOWN and is not replayed because the target may already have received it. Manual runs can overlap; automatic schedules skip occurrences while an earlier automatic run or retry chain is active. Missed downtime occurrences are not backfilled.

Retry count is limited to 0–5, doublings to 0–16, and backoff to 0–86400 seconds. Fractional and explicit zero durations are retained. Retry duration starts with the first actual attempt; when both count and duration are configured both limits must be exhausted. HTTP deadlines are 15–1800 seconds; Pub/Sub ignores attemptDeadline.

Full project/location/job names scope jobs and history. Google-shaped endpoints retain configured gateway IAM enforcement; legacy browse/mutate endpoints retain the existing administrative bypass. Stored IAM policies do not establish per-job enforcement.

History returns at most 100 attempts for an exact owned job and optional since time. The Console loads all job pages before local filtering, then displays 25 jobs per page. Location names are namespaces, not residency guarantees.

services.name: Cloud IAM

persistence.restartBehavior: Audited metadata survives restart while the LocalCloud volume is retained
recoveryLimitations: External runtime/data-plane side effects, if any, have separate lifecycle and recovery limits.

limitations: Open/permissive testIamPermissions echoes requested permissions; strict/gcp-live uses the resolved caller and shared policy evaluator. This is not an arbitrary-principal troubleshooter.

Shared condition evaluation, predefined roles, custom role lifecycle, key enable/disable, and resource-to-project inheritance exist. Full CEL/resource attributes, organization/folder ancestry, deny policies, policy history and recommendations remain incomplete.

Policy API support does not establish uniform data-plane enforcement. In-process Pub/Sub publish and topic deletion do not enforce stored resource bindings; direct external listeners also have service-specific boundaries.

Workforce Identity Pools, SCIM tenant provisioning and Microsoft Active Directory integration are production-only infrastructure features excluded from local development. Workload identity federation is local for OIDC providers only. STS rejects SAML 2.0, AWS GetCallerIdentity and X.509 (mTLS) subjects, access-token downscoping (Credential Access Boundary), actor tokens, options.userProject and workforce-pool audiences with explicit invalid_request errors instead of exchanging them; AWS, SAML and X.509 providers can be stored but never exchange.

OIDC trust keys come from the provider's inline oidc.jwksJson, or from this runtime's own key ring when issuerUri is the LocalCloud issuer. LocalCloud does not fetch remote discovery documents or JWKS, so a remote issuer without jwksJson fails with invalid_grant. HTTP issuerUri values are accepted as a local extension (Google requires HTTPS). Provider CEL supports the standard library, macros and extract(); other extension functions fail to compile. Mapping values are strings or lists of strings, at most 8 KB in total.

Federated principals: the gateway, service-layer IAM evaluator and IAM Credentials resolve principal:// and principalSet:// members from the verified STS token. Cloud KMS keeps its own authorizer and matches only the exact principal:// member, not principalSet:// sets; principalSet:// evaluation through the Cloud Storage authorization callback is unverified. domain: bindings never match federated subjects. The wording of STS error descriptions is LocalCloud's; Google documents only some of them.

google-auth-library-java 1.54.0 accepts only https token_url and service_account_impersonation_url values and a service_account_impersonation.token_lifetime_seconds of 600 to 43200; Java clients need the gateway TLS listener (tls.enabled) and a trusted LocalCloud certificate. Python google-auth 2.57.1 looks the project up at cloudresourcemanager.googleapis.com when an external_account file is loaded with scopes; load it without scopes and call with_scopes.

SDK helpers that hardcode Google hosts cannot use explicit LocalCloud endpoints: impersonated ID tokens in google-auth-library-java 1.54.0 (ImpersonatedCredentials.idTokenWithAudience) and google-auth 2.57.1 (impersonated_credentials.IDTokenCredentials), cloud.google.com/go/auth 0.20.0 credentials/impersonate, and Node google-auth-library 10.5.0 key-file credentials (gtoken 8.0.0 posts to oauth2.googleapis.com). They work through the transparent TLS profile (host.transparent_network, only those hosts mapped to the TLS listener and the LocalCloud CA trusted by the process); explicit alternatives are listed in the SDK guide.

Python google-auth 2.57.1 starts a background Regional Access Boundary lookup at iamcredentials.googleapis.com whenever service-account credentials authorize a request; it cannot be disabled, fails without affecting the call, and is a Google connection unless that host is mapped away.

IAM Credentials tokens are signed by this runtime's issuer. Receivers must trust the local issuer and JWKS; Google-only verifiers that hardcode Google certificates reject them by design. A disabled or deleted account stops LocalCloud's own verification immediately; an external receiver sees revocation only at token expiry. Disabling or deleting an account key stops its JWT-bearer exchanges, self-signed JWT access and publication immediately, but tokens already issued through that key are not tied to it and stay valid, in LocalCloud and at external receivers, until they expire.

In strict and gcp-live every IAM v1 service-account and key method needs the permission Google's REST reference names for it in the stored allow policies, through the shared policy evaluator, for the resolved caller (iam.serviceAccounts.create and list on the project; get, update, delete, enable, disable, undelete, getIamPolicy, setIamPolicy, signBlob and signJwt on the account; iam.serviceAccountKeys.create (also keys.upload) and list on the account; keys get, enable, disable and delete on the key). Open skips the check and permissive logs it. limitations: Locally signed ID and access tokens for projects/-/serviceAccounts/{email-or-uniqueId} with ordered delegates, scopes, includeEmail and organizationNumberIncluded (null; local projects have no organization), lifetimes up to 3600 s or 43200 s for server.identity.lifetime_extension_accounts. In strict and gcp-live every delegation link needs implicitDelegation and the last link the method permission. signBlob and signJwt use one non-exportable SYSTEM_MANAGED key per account, published at /service_accounts/v1/metadata/{x509,jwk}/{email}; IAM v1 signBlob (bytesToSign) and signJwt on a named project keep their v1 shapes on the same paths. A disabled account gets 400 FAILED_PRECONDITION from every method, IAM v1 signing included, and a deleted one 404 NOT_FOUND (IAM Credentials answers PERMISSION_DENIED in strict and gcp-live); invalid base64 or JWT payloads are 400 INVALID_ARGUMENT. Impersonating another project's account needs the grant on that account or its project, not the caller's. organizationNumberIncluded is REST-only, because the gRPC GenerateIdTokenRequest of google-cloud-iamcredentials 2.99.0 has no such field. Served with the Cloud IAM facade. Tokens are signed by the LocalCloud issuer, not Google.

operations.label: sts v1 token (RFC 8693) and iam projects.locations.workloadIdentityPools/providers create/get/list/patch/delete/undelete
limitations: POST /v1/token exchanges an OIDC JWT or ID token (RS256 or ES256, kid required, iat at most 24 hours old) for a locally signed federated access token, as RFC form or Discovery JSON, against a durable OIDC provider of a global workload identity pool. The provider's issuerUri, allowedAudiences (default its canonical name, with or without https:), jwksJson, attributeMapping (CEL; google.subject required, at most 127 bytes; google.groups; attribute.*) and attributeCondition (CEL) decide the exchange. The token's identity is principal://iam.googleapis.com/projects/{number}/locations/global/workloadIdentityPools/{pool}/subject/{subject}, a member of the pool, group and attribute principalSet:// sets; it can call LocalCloud APIs directly and can impersonate a service account through IAM Credentials only with roles/iam.workloadIdentityUser (or another getAccessToken/getOpenIdToken grant) on that account. A disabled provider stops new exchanges; a disabled or deleted pool or a deleted provider also stops existing tokens. Errors are 400 invalid_request, invalid_grant, invalid_target or unsupported_grant_type. Served with the Cloud IAM facade. The pinned Java, Python, Node and Go clients federate subject tokens from file, URL (text and json) and executable credential sources, directly and with service_account_impersonation_url, against the packaged image (integration:identity-sdk-matrix); each SDK runs an executable source only when GOOGLE_EXTERNAL_ACCOUNT_ALLOW_EXECUTABLES=1.

operations.label: services/revisions
limitations: Service/revision metadata and Docker create/update execution exist, with launch-failure rollback tests; broader serving/routing semantics remain partial. CreateService and UpdateService return a pending long-running operation, polled through google.longrunning.Operations or REST GET /v2/projects/{project}/locations/{location}/operations/{operation}. A create reserves the service name (a duplicate gets ALREADY_EXISTS), one deployment runs per service at a time, and a failed first launch releases the name instead of keeping a failed Service resource. With local workload identity, each revision runs behind a localcloud-relay container; its metadata server serves template.serviceAccount (default@{project} when unset, kept when a replacement omits it), and uri is the relay's protected ingress, so the container port is never published (a C24 breaking change in enforcing modes). Ingress follows the IAM mode - open admits anonymous calls, permissive verifies and logs, strict and gcp-live require a local ID token whose aud is the uri or a customAudiences entry (401 otherwise, including access tokens) and run.routes.invoke on the service (403). X-Serverless-Authorization, when present, is the only checked credential and reaches the container without its signature. A Cloud Functions invocation of a function backed by the service is checked at the gateway (cloudfunctions functions.metadata) and reaches the relay with a one-time gateway grant, so the caller's own token reaches the container unchanged. Container.env literal values (v2 env[].value, Knative v1 env[].value) reach the revision container on the direct and relay launch paths, beside the runtime contract's PORT, K_SERVICE, K_REVISION and K_CONFIGURATION, and are stored with the service and each revision, so GET and List Service and Revision return them in the v2 and v1 shapes. UpdateService and Knative replace take the container's env as a whole (a container without env clears it; an update naming no container keeps the serving revision's env, as for its image and port). As in Cloud Run, the four contract names, empty names, names containing '=' or starting with X_GOOGLE_, names or values over 32768 characters or bytes and more than 1000 variables get INVALID_ARGUMENT (HTTP 400 on v1) before anything is reserved. With a workload identity relay, GCE_METADATA_HOST, GCE_METADATA_IP and LOCALCLOUD_RELAY_CAPABILITY are also refused because the relay supplies them (a LocalCloud restriction; Cloud Run does not reserve them). Each revision declares one ADC source on its workload binding - the relay's local metadata (the default), the operator's real credential bridge (gcp_credentials.source adc or service-account, its file mounted read-only at /credentials/gcp.json with GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS, and GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT set to its project), or the template's own GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS, kept unchanged. A template GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS while the bridge is selected is a conflict, and create and update (v2 and Knative v1) get INVALID_ARGUMENT before anything is reserved or launched. GET /browse/cloudrun reports each service's identity.serviceAccount and identity.credentialSource (local, bridge or user). Service and Revision report deployment status from stored revisions, identically over gRPC and REST. A create or update records its revision when admitted and advances generation; each revision settles READY once it serves or FAILED when its launch fails or a restart interrupts it. latestCreatedRevision and latestReadyRevision are full revision names, observedGeneration is the serving revision's generation, and reconciling is true while the latest revision deploys. The Ready terminalCondition and ConfigurationsReady are CONDITION_RECONCILING meanwhile, then CONDITION_SUCCEEDED, or CONDITION_FAILED with reason REVISION_FAILED and the launch error, while the last ready revision keeps serving (RoutesReady). traffic and trafficStatuses report 100 percent TRAFFIC_TARGET_ALLOCATION_TYPE_LATEST once a revision serves. A failed revision's number is not reused. Each Revision reports service, generation 1, observedGeneration 1 once settled, reconciling, a Ready condition and its container port. Knative v1 status (latestCreatedRevisionName, latestReadyRevisionName, observedGeneration, Ready/ConfigurationsReady/RoutesReady with RevisionFailed, traffic) and /browse/cloudrun (latestReadyRevision, latestCreatedRevision, latestCreatedState, reconciling; per revision state and serving) report the same status.
